analysis:
ADMA fell 1.1% to $13.21, outperforming the market by 3.3 percentage points as the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%. The coverage centers on third-quarter results reported yesterday, with headlines indicating earnings and revenues beat estimates, and noting that the company's Asceniv product drove margin improvement. However, the stock's actual move came yesterday – a 26% surge following the after-close earnings report – making today's modest decline more of a consolidation in a sharply down market.

This stock typically makes large moves around earnings, with a median abnormal swing of 9.3% beyond what the market explains, but yesterday's 25.6-point abnormal gain was extraordinary, the largest in the recent pattern. Of the past five beats, three were followed by negative abnormal moves, showing that surpassing estimates hasn't reliably meant the stock rose. Yesterday broke that inconsistency decisively, though whether it marks a change or an outlier won't be clear until the next cycle. The company just reported, so the next earnings date would be approximately three months out.
